Linear: PM-858 Console route toggle UX requirements for quantization
content:
## Background
We’re adding opt-in quantization via the Quantization Profile Library, with **route-level enablement** and **canary rollout** so customers can safely apply quantization only to selected workloads.

This ticket covers Console UX mocks for enabling/disabling quantization on a specific route, selecting a profile strategy, setting canary %, and making it easy to monitor/rollback.

## Goals
- Provide a clear, safe UI to enable quantization on a route, with an explicit warning about potential quality regressions.
- Include canary rollout controls (percentage of traffic) with guardrails and copy that matches rollout semantics.
- Make it easy to jump from configuration to relevant metrics (cost/latency deltas, error rate, quality/regression signals) and audit logs.
- Ensure the UI reflects RBAC constraints: who can change route settings, who can view only.

## Non-goals (for mocks)
- Designing the full profile library browser experience (that’s a separate flow; here we focus on route settings).
- Any per-request override UI (headers/SDK) beyond a small informational callout.

## Primary user
- Platform/ML engineer enabling quantization for a batch summarization route, leaving interactive chat routes untouched.

## Entry points
1) Console → Routes → select a route → Settings tab → “Optimization” / “Quantization” section
2) Console → Model / Optimize → (optional) deep link into route settings (v2; not required for MVP)

## Deliverables
### A) Route settings panel (Quantization section)
Include:
- Section header: “Quantization (Beta)” with short description.
- Toggle: “Enable quantization for this route”
- Read-only “Current execution mode” pill/status (Baseline / Quantized / Mixed (canary) / Unsupported)
- “Profile selection” control:
  - Default: “Auto (recommended)” (Console copy: selects a Redwood-verified profile compatible with current capacity)
  - Advanced: “Pin profile” dropdown (shows profile id + version + precision, e.g., `rwq.llama3-70b.int8.v1.2.0`)
  - Helper text: profile compatibility is hardware-scoped; runtime may fall back.
- Canary control:
  - Slider or stepper: 0%–100% (with common presets 1 / 5 / 10 / 25 / 50 / 100)
  - Copy explains: “% of requests to attempt quantized execution on this route.”
- Guardrails:
  - Inline warning if canary > 0% without monitoring configured (if we can infer).
  - Inline warning if pinned profile is known incompatible with route’s region/capacity class (if we have that signal in UI).

### B) Warning + consent copy
When enabling the toggle (or when moving canary from 0% → >0), show an inline warning and a confirm modal (one-time per route) with:
- “Quantization can reduce cost/latency but may change outputs.”
- Explicit mention of higher risk cases: structured output / JSON mode / tool calling; long context.
- Link: “View acceptance thresholds” (Confluence or docs; placeholder link ok for now).
- Confirm CTA: “Enable with canary” (or “Enable quantization”).

### C) Metrics preview + linkouts
In the Quantization section, include a compact “Monitoring” card with:
- 2–3 metric callouts (mock data ok):
  - Token cost delta (e.g., “-28% vs baseline (24h)”)
  - Latency delta p95 (e.g., “-12% p95 (24h)”)
  - Error rate / fallback rate (e.g., “Fallback 3.1%”) or “Quality regression signals: none / investigating”
- Linkouts:
  - “Open Quantization dashboard” (deep link)
  - “View recent changes (audit log)” (deep link)
  - Optional: “View rollback runbook”

### D) Disabled / unsupported states
Mocks should include:
- Unsupported route (e.g., model not in library): show disabled toggle + reason (“No verified profiles for this model yet.”) and link to “Request support”.
- Insufficient permissions: show read-only view + lock icon + tooltip (“Requires Route Admin”).
- Global org policy disables quantization: show reason and where to change it (Org settings).

## Interaction details to show in mocks
- Enable toggle → confirmation modal (includes warning + canary default suggestion of 5%).
- Canary slider movement triggers: “Save changes” sticky footer with diff summary.
- Pinned profile selection: shows compatibility badge(s) (e.g., “A100/H100 verified”, “L40S not verified”) — may be placeholder data.
- Save action shows toast including whether change is immediate or subject to propagation delay.

## Copy / terminology
- Use “Quantization profile” (not “preset” or “variant”) per docs alignment.
- Use “Fallback to baseline” phrasing, not “fails open.”
- Canary label: “Quantized traffic” rather than “rollout percent” (PM feedback from PM-858).

## Open questions (need input)
1) Do we show a per-route “Quality regression auto-disable enabled” indicator? (Depends on ENG-18503 scope.)
2) Do we allow profile pinning in MVP, or only Auto? (Spec suggests both; PMs leaning Auto-only for beta unless enterprise asks.)
3) Where does the audit log live in Console navigation (Route settings vs Org audit log)? Provide both linkouts?

## Handoff notes
- Provide Figma frames for: default state, enabled w/ 5% canary, pinned profile selected, unsupported state, permission denied state, and confirm modal.
- Include redlines for spacing + component reuse (prefer existing Route Settings patterns: sticky save bar, inline alerts, cards).

## Acceptance criteria
- Mocks cover all states listed above.
- Copy reviewed by PM (Aditya/Nikhil) and SRE (Sean) for safety wording.
- Engineering review confirms controls map to planned backend fields (toggle + canary % + optional pinned profile).

## Links
- Figma: (placeholder) https://figma.com/file/REDWOOD/DES-211-quant-route-controls
- PM requirements: PM-858
comments: 2025-01-30 — Aditya Rao: Please make the warnings very explicit for JSON/tool-calling routes. We keep getting support questions where output formatting breaks first. Also prefer canary defaults to something conservative (5% is fine).
2025-01-31 — Nikhil Sharma: +1 to conservative defaults. Also we should avoid implying quantization is always faster; say “may reduce cost/latency” and point to monitoring.

2025-02-03 — Dylan Brooks: For metrics preview, we can mock the dashboard values but keep the UI aligned with what telemetry will expose (quantized vs baseline tags). Logan/Nadia will confirm which metrics are safe to surface in beta.

2025-02-05 — Sean Gallagher: Please add a clear linkout to rollback guidance + audit log. Also consider an inline callout for “fallback rate” since that’s often the first sign of compatibility issues.
2025-02-06 — Chloe Martin: From Console backend perspective, we’ll likely have: enabled boolean, canaryPercent int, and profilePin optional. UX should show when profilePin is null (“Auto”).
2025-02-07 — Kenji Nakamura: Draft frames are in Figma. Need a decision on whether profile pinning is exposed in beta (currently mocked behind an “Advanced” disclosure).

2025-02-10 — Mina Haddad: Re: wording: avoid “attempt quantized execution” unless we also explain fallback. Suggest: “% of requests routed to quantized execution; incompatible requests will fall back to baseline.”
2025-02-11 — Rafael Mendes: Canary slider should surface that changes can propagate over ~1–2 minutes. Also recommend showing a “last updated by” line for accountability.
